chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
The fig removes bad breath, strengthens the mouth and the bone, promotes hair growth, removes illness, and with it one has no need for medicine.
And he (peace be upon him) said: The fig is most similar to the vegetation of Paradise.
ai.seo_question: What are the health benefits of figs according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) highlights the fig's comprehensive therapeutic value, asserting its efficacy in curing ailments such as halitosis and strengthening the skeletal structure without the need for additional remedies. He further elevates its status by comparing the fig to the vegetation of Paradise, a metaphor that underscores its purity and spiritual significance within Shia tradition, often linking it to the sustenance of the righteous in Jannah.
